problem.h2: Your buyers want to help themselves. You do not want a software project.
problem.lead: Sooner or later, writing orders down by hand stops scaling. The usual answer is a development project. Here is what that choice looks like from the inside:

cards.h3: "We looked into it and gave up"
cards.body: The quotes assumed an IT team we do not have, so the whole idea went back in the drawer and buyers kept calling.

cards.body: A chef with flour on both hands will not hunt through a menu tree. If the new way is slower than calling you, calling you wins.
Service ends long after your office shuts. It sits in voicemail until morning, then somebody writes it out by hand.

faq.h2: Straight answers on portals and VOS

items.q: Is VOS B2B portal software, or something else?
items.a: It does the job distributors buy a portal for: your customers serve themselves, from their own item list, at the prices you gave them, at any hour. It does it through an app they speak to rather than a website they browse, and it holds no storefront, shopping cart or payment handling. Your team's side, where guides and accounts are managed, runs on the web.

items.q: Can our customers order from a web browser?
items.a: Ordering happens on a phone, in the app. The web side is where your own staff edit guides, open accounts and look up past orders. We would rather be plain about that than have you promise your accounts a desktop screen.

items.q: How is this different from a webshop for wholesale?
items.a: A webshop is built around browsing and checkout. A kitchen reordering 40 familiar items every week is not browsing. VOS starts from the guide you built for that account, so the buyer talks through a list they already know, checks it, and sends it. Nothing to search for.

items.q: What does getting started take from our side?
items.a: A guide for every buyer, and a decision on how orders should reach you. That is the whole lift. Unlike B2B portal software you commission, there is nothing to design, host or patch. Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours, and most of their customers send something in that same day.

items.q: Will orders drop into the system we already run?
items.a: Yes. Orders can arrive as a PDF, Excel or Word attachment, through EDI, into QuickBooks, or over an API link to whatever platform your office runs on. On the EDI, QuickBooks and API routes nobody enters it a second time. Emailed files may still be keyed in, which is worth weighing when you choose.

items.q: Do you take on B2B customer portal development for us?
items.a: No. We are not an agency and we do not take build work, custom front-ends, or bespoke integrations beyond the delivery formats listed above. VOS is a finished product you switch on. If what you need really is a bespoke portal, a development shop is the right call, not us.

items.q: We were looking for B2B travel portal software. Is this it?
items.a: No. Travel portals book flights, hotels and cars out of global distribution systems, and VOS does none of that. VOS serves food distributors who supply restaurants and grocery stores. If you arrived here after travel booking, this is the wrong product.

items.q: What happens to accounts that keep phoning?
items.a: Nothing breaks. Your team writes those up the way it does today, and those calls carry no VOS number or timestamp. A sensible start is the customers who order most often, then let the rest follow once they see it working.

items.q: Are we too small for this?
items.a: No. VOS exists for exactly that kind of operation, with no IT department required. You need no developer, no IT staff and no project plan. Pricing is quoted per distributor, so ask us what it looks like at your account count.
